title: I came to study
goal: Use -mAk with the dative and the ablative, and say why you go somewhere with -mAgA and -mAk üçin.

intro.text: Some verbs take `-mAk` in the dative, *-maga* or *-mäge*: *okamaga başladym* (I started reading), *gelmäge synanyşdy* (he tried to come). The same dative gives a purpose after a verb of going: *Men okamaga geldim* (I came to study). *Gorkmak* and *ýadamak* take the ablative: *ýüzmekden gorkýar*.

vocab.en: to try (with the dative: gelmäge synanyşmak, to try to come)
to get tired; to be tired (of: with -dan)
to give up, to quit; to throw away
to earn; to win (pul gazanmak: to earn money)

exercises.question: How do you say **she started singing**?

why.2: *-dan* is the ablative. *Başlamak* takes the dative: *aýtmaga*.

exercises.text: Merjen türkmençe gürle___ synanyşýar, ýöne ýalňyşmak___ gorkýar.
exercises.en: Merjen tries to speak Turkmen, but she's afraid of making mistakes.

accept: mäge

reject.why: After a front vowel the dative of `-mAk` is *-mäge*, with ä: *gürlemäge*.

exercises.gloss: (went) to work, in order to work
exercises.explain: The dative of `-mAk` after a front vowel is *-mäge*: *işlemäge*.

accept: Men okamaga geldim.
Okamaga geldim.
(Men) okamak üçin geldim.

reject.why: For a purpose after *gelmek*, use the dative: *okamaga geldim*.
*Okamagy* is the accusative. For a purpose: *okamaga geldim*.

exercises.explain: After a verb of coming, `-mAgA` gives the purpose: *okamaga geldim*.

accept: We went to the market to buy fruit.
We went to the bazaar to buy fruit.
We went to the [market|bazaar] to get (some) fruit.
We went to the [market|bazaar] to buy some fruit.
He got tired of waiting and left.
She got tired of waiting and left.
[He|She] got tired of waiting and [went|went away].
[He|She] was tired of waiting and [left|went away].
üçin

exercises.explain: `-mAk üçin` gives a purpose after any verb: *pul gazanmak üçin*.

exercises.question: Which verb completes *Merjen ýüzmekden ___.*?
exercises.explain: *Gorkmak* takes the ablative, as with a noun: *ýüzmekden gorkýar*.

exercises.prompt: I have no time to read.
accept: Okamaga wagtym ýok.
Meniň okamaga wagtym ýok.
Mende okamaga wagt ýok.

reject.why: What the time is for takes the dative: *okamaga wagtym ýok*.

exercises.explain: The dative says what the time is for: *okamaga wagtym ýok*.

exercises.prompt: Türkmen dilini öwrenmek üçin her gün kitap okaýaryn.
accept: I read books every day to learn Turkmen.
I read a book every day to learn Turkmen.
To learn Turkmen, I read books every day.
Every day I read books to learn Turkmen.
I read books every day in order to learn Turkmen.
In order to learn Turkmen, I read books every day.

exercises.question: **Aýna got up to drink some water.** Which is right?

why.1: *Içmegi* is the accusative. For a purpose after *turmak*: *içmäge*.
why.2: The bare `-mAk` doesn't show purpose here: *içmäge turdy*.

exercises.explain: After a verb of movement, the dative gives the purpose: *suw içmäge turdy*.

accept: Düşünmäge synanyşýarys.
